findings.summary: sanitize_label(None) returns None instead of the empty string the task requires, still risking a crash in callers.
findings.mechanism: The new guard `if text is None: return` has no return value, so it implicitly returns None (not ""). The task brief explicitly requires 'label sanitization ... should accept a None value and treat it as an empty string.' Any caller that does `_html.escape(sanitize_label(x))` or otherwise treats the result as a string (e.g. export.py:408 `_html.escape(sanitize_label((community_labels or {}).get(cid, ...)))`) will still crash with TypeError if a None flows through, since html.escape/string concatenation don't accept None.
